text:
maria: FYI noticed weird spikes in queue depth for us-west-2 around 03:12 UTC, autoscaler kept flapping when batch_size dropped to 1-2 and tail latency shot up. screenshots in dashboard thread.
prateek: Saw that earlier too. looks like short-lived network egress blips are causing pods to fail readiness for ~10-30s, LB strips connections and queue pushes to remaining replicas -> batch collapse.
maria: here's the main Grafana panel query I'm using (Prometheus):
```
sum(rate(inference_queue_depth_total[1m])) by (cluster,region)
```
but it's noisy. p99 queue depth hits 600 then back to 50 in 2m.
tessa: noisy metrics are the crux. we should move from instant to a smoothed quantile (p95 over 5m sliding) and alert on sustained (>3m) p95 > threshold. also add a "batch_drop_rate" derived metric so we can alert on batch size truncation instead of queue alone.
prateek: agree. proposed recording rule for batch_drop_rate:
```
- record: infra:batch_drop_rate:rate5m
  expr: sum(increase(inference_batches_dropped_total[5m])) / sum(increase(inference_batches_total[5m]))
```
then expose in grafana as a sparklines + single stat.
sam: can we also compute "inverse_headroom"? headroom = capacity_tokens - queued_tokens; inverse_headroom = 1/(headroom+1) so small headroom -> large signal, easier to threshold. avoids spiky positives when capacity is huge.
maria: nice. inverse is good for proportional alerts that scale across fleets. sample promql: 
```
rate_capacity = sum(increase(inference_serving_capacity_tokens[5m]))
rate_queue = sum(increase(inference_queue_tokens[5m]))
infra:inverse_headroom:5m = (rate_queue / (rate_capacity - rate_queue + 1))
```
(not exact syntax, just the idea)
june: caution: inverse can blow up when capacity ~ queue. debounce with max clamp: clamp_max(..., 1000). and add a time window check so a single 10s blip doesn't fire.
prateek: for alerts i'm proposing: 
- P0 alert: infra:inverse_headroom:5m > 0.2 for 10m AND infra:batch_drop_rate:rate5m > 0.05 for 2m -> page on-call.
- P1 alert (warning): infra:inverse_headroom:5m > 0.15 for 5m -> slack channel notify.
This ties a headroom signal to actual batch drops so we don't page on noise.
tessa: add region filter: only page if it affects >1 AZ or >20% of serving capacity. prevents single-node weirdness from pagers.
sam: operational note: increasing min_replicas from 3->5 in us-west reduces flapping but costs ~+12% in that fleet. still cheaper than repeated failovers causing 3x token-cost during retries. we should model both.
maria: cost model: calculate 3 scenarios (keep current, bump min_replicas, add readiness-probe backoff). which teams should own the cost calc? ops or infra? prateek volunteered.
prateek: i'll run a quick back-of-envelope + write a short dashboard comparing egress errors vs queue depth, and add a cost overlay (est tokens lost * $/token). will post later today.
ops-bot: deploy-notify: dashboard/queue-insights updated by prateek at 1912000200
june: small UX ask: can we add an annotations stream to the headroom panel showing autoscaler actions and node add/removes so correlation is immediate? grafana has an events datasource; we can pipe k8s events.
maria: agreed. action items:
- prateek: add recording rules for batch_drop_rate and inverse_headroom + update dashboard panels (ETA today)
- tessa: propose alert thresholds & debounce policy in pagerduty (ETA tomorrow)
- sam: run cost tradeoff simulation for min_replicas change (ETA EOD)
- june: wire k8s events to grafana annotations (ETA next week)
If no objections i'll turn on the new alert as warning first then escalate to paging if stable. :thumbsup:
prateek: adding note: also check for network egress shaping in the region (AWS notices) — last week they had transient routing issues that match the times.
maria: ok lets reconvene after prateek's dashboard link. thanks all :heart:
